Scene: Demo street (the name as typed)
Exact sheet. For the owner's own use: everything on the Aggregate sheet, plus a map with every camera's position and coverage, camera labels and the
walls each camera sees per building. It shows where cameras are: do not share it without the agreement of everyone whose camera is on it.
Every figure here is an estimate from a model of the street, not a record of what any camera films. Read them as "up to": see what the figures leave

g.text: ESTIMATE · modelled from map data, not recorded footage
SHOWS CAMERA POSITIONS · for the owner's own use

svg.text: Seen at Detect (25 px/m) by day:
Numbered dots are cameras, with a line in the direction each faces; diamonds are targets (T1, T2, …); dashed outlines are the areas as drawn, coloured by label. North is
up. Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL). Elevation: USGS 3DEP via the demo fixtures
4 cameras are enabled. Ranges are at Detect (25 px/m), from each model's published resolution and field of view. Labels are as the user typed them.
What the enabled cameras together can see, at every detail level by day and by night, with the area each figure is out of. No single figure stands for
the whole: the higher the detail asked for, the less ground any camera covers.

The street by kind, at Detect (25 px/m) (see what “street” means)
Up to: trees, hedges, fences and vehicles are not counted. 'Street' includes driveways and footpaths.
Each camera's visible ground at Detect (25 px/m) by day, split by the areas drawn and labelled in the scene. Areas and labels are as drawn by the user,
not property boundaries. A label figure is given as drawn, with below it the range it takes when every outline is moved 1 m in and 1 m out. Areas may
overlap, so the columns need not add up.
Ground and walls each camera sees, m² (labels as drawn)
Areas as drawn (names as the user typed them)
Front garden: Own, outline 256 m² as drawn; ground seen by Camera 1 · House 1 front: 87 m² (76–89).
Next door: Neighbour, outline 256 m² as drawn; ground seen by Camera 1 · House 1 front: 1 m² (0–4).
Walls seen per building (buildings by their number in the loaded map)
Camera 1 · House 1 front: building 94 at 3 m: 3 m²; building 101 at 8 m: 5 m².
Camera 2 · House 2 front: building 51 at 21 m: 89 m²; building 64 at 29 m: 44 m²; building 53 at 32 m: 69 m².
Camera 3 · House 3 front: building 106 at 7 m: 72 m².
For each target, whether the model rules out that each camera sees it. ✓ not ruled out: some of the target is visible in the model. ✗ ruled out, for the
reason given. The wording is one-sided because hedges, fences, trees and vehicles are not modelled and can only block more. Target names are as the user
At Detect (25 px/m) by day: not ruled out for Camera 1 · House 1 front; ruled out for 3: outside the view (2), out of range (1).
Camera 1 · House 1 front: by day Detect ✓, Observe ✓, Recognise ✗ (out of range), Identify ✗ (out of range); at night Detect ✓, Observe ✓, Recognise ✗ (out of range),
Street is the ground on every road, path and service way mapped in OpenStreetMap whose highway type is one of these, each as a band of the width in
brackets centred on the mapped line: motorway, trunk (14 m); primary (10 m); secondary (8 m); tertiary (7 m); residential, unclassified (6 m);
living_street (5 m); service (4 m); footway, path, pedestrian, cycleway, steps (2 m); motorway_link, trunk_link, primary_link, secondary_link,
tertiary_link (6 m). A way tagged with a width of at least 1 m and below 60 m uses that width; failing that, a lanes tag of at least 1 and below 12
gives 3.25 m a lane. Ground under a building is never street.
Carriageway is the street on every type above but service, footway, path, pedestrian, cycleway and steps. Footpath and service is the rest of the
street: ground on one of those and on no carriageway. Driveways are usually mapped as service ways, so they count here.
A spot counts as seen by a camera when a point 1.0 m above the ground there (the subject height) lies inside the camera's field of view and within its
range, and the straight line from the camera to it passes through no building and stays clear of the ground. Ground is tested at the centre of every 0.5
m square cell outside buildings, walls in patches of about 1 m. A figure is the area of the cells or patches seen.
Range at a detail level of D pixels per metre is R = W ÷ (2 × D × tan(H ÷ 2)), where W is the camera's published horizontal resolution in pixels and H
its horizontal field of view (taken as at most 170°), and never more than 100 m. At night R is also no more than the camera's published infrared range,
or 7.5 m where none is published. The detail levels (DORI, after EN 62676-4) are Detect 25 px/m (can tell someone is there), Observe 62 px/m (can follow
what someone does and wears), Recognise 125 px/m (can recognise someone already known) and Identify 250 px/m (can identify a stranger, beyond doubt);
Custom is a density the user sets.
Areas and their labels (own, neighbour, public, other) are outlines the user drew, as drawn: they are not property boundaries, and no property data is
used. Each area figure is given as drawn, with the range it takes when every outline is moved 1 m in and 1 m out, and each outline's own area is printed
beside it. The scene, area and target names are printed as the user typed them.
A verdict on a target is one-sided. Not ruled out: some of the target is visible in the model. Ruled out: the model rules it out, for the reason given.
What the model leaves out can only block more, so it never says that a camera sees a place.
What the figures leave out (caveats version 1)
Not modelled: trees, hedges, fences and walls, vehicles, poles, street furniture, awnings, bridges and tunnels. Cameras see straight through them, so
the figures can only overstate what is visible past them.
Buildings come from OpenStreetMap. One missing from the map lets cameras see through the gap; one demolished but still mapped blocks a view that is
Building heights are inferred where they are not tagged, and roofs are flat, so views over and onto buildings can be wrong in either direction.
Terrain is approximate: ground heights come from a public elevation model sampled every 5 m, so small banks, retaining walls and cuttings are
'Street' includes driveways and footpaths: every mapped road, service road and footpath counts, as a band of estimated width.
Detail levels are pixel-density targets from the published resolution, not a test of what a camera records. Range is capped at 100 m, and floodlights
and street lights are ignored at night.
Only the loaded area is analysed, at one subject height: views beyond its edge are cut off.
Leaving these out can only overstate what a camera sees, so read the figures as "up to". Inferred heights and missing or out-of-date buildings err in
both directions, though, so they are not a strict upper bound.
